recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless CDS opens a new issue to revise DetectedIssue mitigation examples more broadly.
issue_request: FHIR-5260 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 CDS ballot comment against FHIR-core-Alert/Contraindication. It found the example 'Noting that a duplicate therapy is actually intended' confusing and asked for clarification. The approved resolution was to expand the example so a duplicate-therapy contraindication/issue is submitted along with mitigation indicating the duplication was intended or managed.
initial_application: SVN #5120, preserved as git commit e0375fb4ccceb176a0150b77007f07a62c0cca6c, changed source/contraindication/contraindication-introduction.xml from the ambiguous sentence to an order-submission example with a link to a duplicate-therapy contraindication and mitigation.
additional_context: FHIR-8043 renamed Contraindication to DetectedIssue while retaining Contraindication as an alias; commit 1408563d743f15eff785f59063b34b538b4d4651 carried the clarified text into source/detectedissue/detectedissue-introduction.xml using 'issue' terminology. source/fhir.ini actively lists detectedissue=DetectedIssue and marks DetectedIssue approved, while source/alert and source/contraindication are absent in the current checkout. Community searches found no FHIR-5260-specific or conflicting Zulip/Confluence guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already states that a clinician may submit a new order including a link to a 'duplicate therapy' issue with mitigation indicating the therapy is not considered duplicate, preserving the approved clarification.

related_jiras.note: Renamed Contraindication to DetectedIssue and explains why the FHIR-5260 wording now appears in DetectedIssue rather than Alert/Contraindication.
